claim: Computing is largely invisible and embedded throughout surroundings.
originalWording: Computing is largely invisible and embedded throughout surroundings.

sources.title: Spiritual Machines: The Merging of Man and Machine — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: Computers and communications in 2019: embedded computers

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source and full record for attribution limits.

reference.criterion: Computing is commonly embedded unobtrusively in everyday objects and systems, rather than confined to visibly separate PCs.
reference.rationale: Wearables, household robots and networked systems show that embedded computing had become a normal part of surroundings by 2019. The reference treats “everywhere” as pervasive integration, not a requirement to implant computers in every chair, wall or person.

strict.criterion: Every listed setting—walls, furniture, clothing, jewelry and bodies—has become a common computing location.
strict.rationale: The product categories are unevenly realized, especially ordinary clothing and elective in-body computing. This full-list reading remains partial.
